text: This is the inverse image of L.carrier under the subtype inclusion Lᵛ→V. Integrality already gives L⊆Lᵛ, so it is the genuine embedded denominator needed to form Lᵛ/L in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). It does not quotient the entire ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L65) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L77) passes.
Membership is exactly original-carrier membership of the underlying ambient vector.
Mapping the denominator back to V recovers L.carrier exactly.

The submodule is precisely {x∈V | B(x,L)⊆ℤ}, by [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). For nondegenerate B this realizes the integral dual in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). Keeping it as a submodule is necessary: its self-pairings need not be integral, and without nondegeneracy it need not be finitely generated. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Discriminant.lean#L40) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Finiteness.lean#L134) passes.
For nonzero Gram parameter a the dual is (1/a)ℤ.
The dual is a full finitely generated lattice exactly in the nondegenerate case.

The type is the actual quotient of the ambient dual submodule by the embedded original carrier. Under nondegeneracy the dual identifies with Homℤ(L,ℤ), giving exactly the discriminant group of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Its broader definition makes no finiteness assertion for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L112) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L132) passes.
A dual representative gives zero precisely when it lies in the original carrier.
The finite-group condition is exactly nondegeneracy.

A class in Lᵛ/L is zero exactly when its representative belongs to the denominator. Unfolding carrierInDual makes that membership x∈L.carrier in V, exactly the quotient interpretation in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L118) passes.
The general equality criterion uses a difference in the same original carrier.

Nondegeneracy makes Lᵛ a finite free integer module of the same rank as L. Its full-rank submodule L therefore has finite quotient by [Mathlib’s full-rank quotient theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/Finite/Quotient.lean#L96), agreeing with the finiteness assertion in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). The premise is essential. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L132) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Discriminant.lean#L178) passes.
The converse characterizes precisely when finiteness holds.
For nonzero rank-one parameter a the quotient has |a| elements.

carrierInDual is the submodule pulled back to the dual subtype, so membership is definitionally membership of the underlying ambient vector in L. This identifies the precise denominator of the quotient in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L77) passes.
The image of this pulled-back denominator is exactly the original carrier.

The dual carrier is the integer span of the bilinear dual of a finite rational basis. That span is finitely generated and rationally spans V, giving the stated IsLattice instance. Nondegeneracy supplies the dual basis, as in [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L83) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Finiteness.lean#L134) passes.
The dual carrier equals the integral span of the explicit rational dual basis.
The full-lattice conclusion has exactly the required nondegeneracy boundary.

The embedded denominator and the original carrier are integrally linearly equivalent by forgetting or adding the dual-membership proof. Their integer finranks therefore agree. This preserves the copy of L in the quotient construction of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7), without requiring nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L96) passes.
Transporting a carrier basis leaves its underlying vectors unchanged.

The image consists of the vectors lying in both L and Lᵛ; integrality gives L⊆Lᵛ, so this intersection is exactly L. It verifies that the denominator in the quotient of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7) is the original lattice, not a larger submodule. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L112) passes.
Vanishing of a quotient class tests membership in that exact original carrier.

Coordinates in the rational bilinear dual basis are the pairings with the original basis vectors. Pairing integrally with L therefore means precisely that these coordinates are integers, giving the displayed span equality by [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Nondegeneracy is retained. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Discriminant.lean#L58) passes.
For Gram parameter a≠0 the formula specializes to the integer span of 1/a.

The nondegenerate dual carrier is a full integer lattice in V; its integer basis extends to a rational basis of V. Thus its rank is dimℚ V, consistent with the dual-module identification in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L194) passes.
The transported dual-carrier basis is the actual ambient bilinear dual basis.

This equality exposes the definition: carrierInDual is L.carrier restricted to the dual-carrier subtype. It supplies the actual denominator L used in Lᵛ/L, as in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7); no nondegeneracy or finite-index claim is introduced. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L77) passes.
The denominator maps back onto the original carrier.

Two classes in an additive quotient agree exactly when the difference of their representatives lies in the denominator. The subtype coercion then gives the displayed ambient-carrier criterion, precisely the coset relation in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L112) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Discriminant.lean#L172) passes.
Taking the second representative zero recovers the kernel criterion.
In the rank-one model, class representatives become the corresponding integer residues.

The quantified integrality condition is membership in the dual of Lᵛ. Nondegenerate symmetric double duality identifies that submodule with L, exactly the bidual interpretation supplied by [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). The nondegeneracy premise is explicit. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L219) passes.
The underlying submodule equality identifies the double dual with the original carrier.

The inclusion is exactly the stored integrality condition: each x∈L pairs integrally with every y∈L. By [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), that is membership in Lᵛ. No nondegeneracy is required for this inclusion. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Discriminant.lean#L40) passes.
For nonzero integer parameter a the familiar inclusion ℤ⊆(1/a)ℤ is recovered.

Dualizing once with B and then with B.flip recovers the full lattice; symmetry identifies B.flip with B. This proves the stated nondegenerate symmetric double-dual equality, using [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), while keeping the dual as an ambient submodule. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L226) passes.
Membership in the double dual is exactly original-carrier membership.

The construction transports b along the inverse of the canonical integral equivalence from the embedded denominator to L. Hence it is a basis of the copy of L inside Lᵛ, not a basis of all Lᵛ. This is the denominator used in [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L96) passes.
Each transported vector is the original bi with its dual-membership proof.

The integral functional dual basis is transported through the inverse of Lᵛ≃Homℤ(L,ℤ). Its vectors are therefore the ambient bilinear dual basis, the dual realization described in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4) and [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L194) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L166) passes.
The transported basis agrees with the ambient dual-basis vectors.
The pairing equivalence sends each such vector to the matching functional dual basis vector.

The first dual pairs in the first argument of B; the outside flip makes the second dual use the opposite argument. Nondegeneracy and the dual-basis computation recover the original full carrier, precisely the flipped bidual identity in [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L219) passes.
Symmetry specializes the flipped identity to ordinary double duality.

An integral functional is represented by the sum of its basis values times the rational bilinear dual basis. This vector lies in Lᵛ; nondegeneracy gives uniqueness. Thus the map is exactly the integral-dual identification used in [Dolgachev §1.2](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=4), without requiring L itself unimodular. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L166) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L135) passes.
The equivalence matches bilinear dual-basis vectors with integral coordinate functionals.
Its values cast to the original rational bilinear pairing.

Transporting b to the copy of L inside Lᵛ only adds the proof that bi belongs to the dual carrier. Forgetting the outer subtype gives exactly the displayed dual vector. This preserves the denominator embedding in the quotient of [Nikulin §1.3](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=7). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Discriminant/Group.lean#L77) passes.
Forgetting all subtype wrappers recovers the original lattice in V.

The dual-carrier basis was transported from the functional dual basis along the inverse pairing equivalence. Coordinates therefore transport back along that equivalence, giving exactly the displayed repr equality. The coordinate interpretation follows from [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L166) passes.
Each dual-carrier basis vector maps to its corresponding coordinate functional.

The equivalence has the ordinary integral dual-pairing map as its underlying map. Casting that integer value gives B(x,y), exactly the pairing normalization in [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). Nondegeneracy makes the map bijective; it does not change its values. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L114) passes.
The underlying pairing already has this exact cast equation.

A dual vector x defines the integer functional y↦B(x,y), since dual membership ensures integrality. Injectivity of ℤ→ℚ gives the linear laws, as in [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40). This definition needs no nondegeneracy; bijectivity is asserted separately. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L114) passes.
Casting the functional value recovers the exact ambient pairing.

Bundling the dual pairing as an equivalence adds its bijectivity proof while retaining the same linear map. The equality therefore identifies the equivalence with precisely the pairing in [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), rather than an arbitrary dual-module isomorphism. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L135) passes.
The equivalence retains the original rational pairing on every pair of vectors.

The chosen integer pairing value is specified by its image being B(x,y); dual membership guarantees such an integer and injectivity of the cast makes it unique. This is exactly the specification of [Mathlib’s dual-submodule pairing](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/DualLattice.lean#L40), including for degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean#L135) passes.
In the nondegenerate case, bundling an equivalence preserves the same cast equation.

The difference c♯(x)−1⊗x vanishes on V(I)×G exactly when subgroup points conjugate every ambient point trivially, matching [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). Published [whole-group](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Central/Basic.lean#L113) and [identity-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Central/Basic.lean#L253) controls pass. The subgroup occupies the first tensor factor; the condition uses all coordinates x and keeps nonreduced structure.
The whole group is central exactly when its Hopf algebra is cocommutative.
The identity closed subgroup is central without ambient cocommutativity.

If I≤J, the left tensor ideal grows, so every conjugation defect vanishing modulo I also vanishes modulo J. This matches subgroup containment in the center in [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). The published [supremum control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Central/Basic.lean#L107) passes. Centrality is upward closed in ideal order because larger ideals define smaller subgroups.
A join is central if one summand is, testing upward ideal-order closure.

For I=0, centrality says conjugation is the second projection, hence the two universal tensor points commute. Their products are Δ and its flip under [Milne’s convolution dictionary](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). The published [universal-point control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/CentralPoint.lean#L264) passes. The resulting condition is cocommutativity, not the already assumed commutativity of the coordinate ring.
Commutativity of the two universal tensor points is exactly cocommutativity.

Evaluating the conjugation defect at a subgroup point and any ambient point gives ghg⁻¹=h, also after changing value algebra, as required by [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). The published [universal-test control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/CentralPoint.lean#L230) passes. IsCentralPoint quantifies over further value algebras; commuting only with the original A-points would be weaker.
Universal tensor-valued point detects centrality after every value-algebra extension.

The forward implication evaluates conjugation defects; the converse tests the universal subgroup and ambient points in (H/I)⊗H. This realizes [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44) without reducing to field points. Published [whole-group](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Central/Basic.lean#L113) and [identity-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Central/Basic.lean#L253) controls pass. The quotient tensor-kernel identity needs no flatness assumption.
The whole group is central exactly when its Hopf algebra is cocommutative.
The identity closed subgroup is central without ambient cocommutativity.

Every point vanishing on a central ideal stays commuting after all value-algebra maps, so it lies in the functorial center of [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). Published [abstract-center containment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/CentralPoint.lean#L206) and [value-change](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/CentralPoint.lean#L216) controls pass. The target is HopfAlgebra.center, whose condition is stronger than membership in the abstract center of G(A).
Functorial center is contained in the abstract point-group center.
Functorial centrality is preserved by value-algebra maps.

The augmentation ideal cuts out only the identity point, which remains central under every value-algebra map, as in [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). The published [identity-subgroup control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L212) passes. This uses the counit kernel, not the zero ideal; no cocommutativity of the ambient Hopf algebra is required.
The augmentation ideal cuts out only the identity point.

Central subgroup points commute with every ambient point, so conjugation fixes them and preserves the subgroup, matching [Milne, Proposition 1.92](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=44). The published [kernel-normality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L72) passes, using centrality of augmentation as a concrete instance of this implication. All-algebra-valued normality recovers the coordinate condition; no flatness is needed.
Extension of central augmentation gives a normal group-kernel ideal.

Points of a central subgroup commute with one another; injective quotient-point inclusion detects this for the two universal points. Their convolution products encode Δ and its flip by [Milne’s convolution dictionary](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=75). Published [cocommutativity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/CentralPoint.lean#L264) and [inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L104) controls pass. Cocommutativity is proved for H/I, not necessarily for H.
Commutativity of the two universal tensor points is exactly cocommutativity.
Quotient-point inclusion is injective for every value algebra.

The inclusion c♯(I)⊆H⊗I says conjugation preserves V(I), with the acted-on subgroup in the second factor, matching [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). Published [whole-group](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L122) and [ring-valued-point](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L252) controls pass. Lean’s algebraic predicate extends to commutative semirings; the tensor ideal is a generated image, without an injective tensor-embedding assumption.
The zero ideal defining the whole group is normal over commutative semirings.
The coordinate condition is equivalent to all-value-algebra normality over rings.

The equivalence exposes the defining inclusion of the ideal generated by c♯(I) into the right tensor ideal, the coordinate version of [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). Published [elementwise](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L78) and [zero-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L122) controls pass. The map is an algebra morphism for conjugation, not a claimed Hopf morphism of the product group.
Generated ideal containment is equivalent to membership of each conjugated generator.
The zero ideal defining the whole group is normal over commutative semirings.

Containment of the generated ideal image is equivalent to containment of every generator c♯(x), yielding the normality criterion of [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [conjugation-evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101) passes. Quantification is over x∈I, and the right tensor ideal places the subgroup in the acted-on factor; commutative semirings suffice.
Evaluation of c♯ at two points is ghg⁻¹ in the documented order.

Applying the normality inclusion to the generator x∈I places c♯(x) in the right tensor ideal, as required by [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [point-normality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L188) passes over commutative rings and uses precisely this membership to evaluate conjugates. The underlying membership lemma itself only requires commutative semirings.
Coordinate normality gives a normal subgroup over each value algebra.

Naturality of conjugation carries the defining inclusion through f⊗f, so extension of a normal ideal remains normal. Contravariantly this is inverse image of a normal subgroup, as in [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [augmentation-extension control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L72) passes. No surjectivity of f or tensor injectivity is assumed; ideal.map means generated image.
Extension of central augmentation gives a normal group-kernel ideal.

The zero ideal has zero conjugation image, so its normality inclusion holds. It cuts out the whole ambient group, which normalizes itself in [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [whole-point-group control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) passes over rings. The algebraic zero-ideal proof works already over commutative semirings without any cocommutativity requirement.
The zero ideal cuts out the whole ambient point group.

Evaluation of c♯(I)⊆H⊗I at (g,n), with n vanishing on I, makes gng⁻¹ vanish on I. This is normality on all algebra-valued points in [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). Published [conjugation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Hopf/Conjugation.lean#L101) and [normal-quotient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Presheaf.lean#L83) controls pass. The value algebra is arbitrary, with no density, reducedness or field assumption.
Evaluation of c♯ at two points is ghg⁻¹ in the documented order.
The quotient by a normal cut-out subgroup has exactly that subgroup as kernel.

Normality of all point subgroups is detected by the universal pair in H⊗(H/I); their conjugate recovers c♯(I)⊆H⊗I, matching [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [kernel-normality control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L72) passes. The converse uses the kernel of id⊗q for a quotient map, so right exactness suffices and no flatness or rational-point density is needed.
Extension of central augmentation gives a normal group-kernel ideal.

A bijective coordinate map gives equivalences of point groups, carrying the cut-out subgroup and conjugation to their counterparts; normality is therefore invariant, as in [Milne, §1.j](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=42). The published [membership-transport control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L247) passes. Both injectivity and surjectivity are explicit; this does not claim normality survives arbitrary schematic images.
Membership in the cut-out subgroup transports through the surjective coordinate map.

Subgroup closure over every value algebra gives the Hopf laws via universal points: multiplication over (H/I)⊗(H/I), inversion over H/I and the identity detect comultiplication, antipode and counit. This implements [Milne, §1.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=19) and [Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). Published [unchanged-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Representability.lean#L88) and [centralizer-application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/Centralizer/Basic.lean#L220) controls pass. Quotient right exactness avoids flatness; the equations already force naturality.
The constructed Hopf ideal retains the original defining ideal.
Published centralizer construction has the intended universal commutation equations.

Forgetting the constructed Hopf structure returns exactly the supplied ideal I, preserving the closed subscheme in [Milne, §1.5](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=19) and [Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The published [universal-normalizer application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/Normalizer/Scheme.lean#L299) passes and uses this equality to recover its defining equations. No radical, closure or enlargement of I is introduced; subgroup data certify the existing ideal.
Published normalizer construction has exactly its universal normalization equations.

For positive p, this identifies the fundamental group of ℝ/pℤ with the additive integers, written multiplicatively. The covering translation is converted from the opposite group using commutativity. The source’s n-turn loop has winding number n, fixing the positive orientation and ruling out a sign-reversed isomorphism. Its basepoint-lift choice is removed by the existing commutative-covering independence theorem. Compared with [Chapter 1 §5, pp.8–9, circle fundamental group and lifted-endpoint inverse](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/FundamentalGroupCircle.lean#L49).

The function takes a based loop homotopy class to the integer underlying its winding-number isomorphism. Thus it is well-defined on classes, rather than on a choice of real lift. The existing displacement formula and n-turn evaluation identify it with the standard integer winding count after rescaling the covering by the positive period p. Compared with [Chapter 1 §5, p.9, j on loop classes and j[fₙ]=n](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/FundamentalGroupCircle.lean#L56).

For any continuous real lift of the based loop, its endpoint difference lies in pℤ; dividing by p gives the winding integer. Subtracting f(0) makes the formula valid for any initial lift, not only one starting at zero. The displayed equality is in ℝ after coercing that integer, and positive p makes division legitimate. Compared with [Chapter 1 §5, p.9, lifted-endpoint winding; translated and rescaled here](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/FundamentalGroupCircle.lean#L61).

This is the product-coordinate homeomorphism y↦(y(i),y restricted to j≠i). Its inverse restores the selected coordinate and all remaining coordinates. It isolates exactly one interval factor, as required by the cubical loop construction, and the product-topology argument works for arbitrary index types, not only finite cubes. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, cube as a product of intervals; coordinate splitting checked directly in the pinned source](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L67).

The inverse coordinate homeomorphism sends (t,y) to the cube point with coordinate i equal to t and all other coordinates supplied by y. The complement is the subtype j≠i, so no coordinate is duplicated or omitted. Continuity follows coordinatewise in the product topology, with no finiteness premise. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, product cube and coordinate-face convention; inverse formula checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L72).

Insertion lands on a coordinate face when either the inserted interval coordinate is an endpoint or a remaining coordinate is an endpoint. The proof selects i in the first case and the corresponding complementary index in the second. This is exactly the boundary condition needed to curry a based cubical map. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, boundary means at least one endpoint coordinate](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L75).

An index equivalence reindexes cube coordinates: the image of p is y↦p(y∘e), with inverse using e⁻¹. The existential face condition is preserved in both directions, and precomposition gives continuous maps on the compact-open subspaces. Hence the result correctly bundles a homeomorphism of generalized-loop spaces, before quotienting by homotopy. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, coordinate cubical model; reindexing and compact-open continuity checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L161).

Uncurrying a loop of complementary generalized loops gives y↦p(y(i))(y restricted to j≠i). A boundary face in coordinate i uses the outer loop’s constant endpoints; a face in any other coordinate uses the inner boundary condition. Joint continuity follows from evaluation on the compact Hausdorff complementary cube. Compared with [Proposition A.14(a),(c), pp.530–531, evaluation and uncurrying](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L287).

For any empty index type, the cube is a point and has no boundary condition. Evaluation identifies its generalized maps with all points of X; a relative homotopy becomes exactly a path between those values. The quotient congruence converts both relations explicitly, so the result is a set equivalence with all path components. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, zero cube and π₀ as path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L474).

The lemma exposes the defining requirement of a generalized loop: at every cube point having an endpoint coordinate, its value is the chosen basepoint. It applies to all points of every face, not just vertices, which is precisely the boundary condition in the cubical model. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, maps of the pair (Iⁿ,∂Iⁿ) to (X,x)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L142).

The setoid uses precisely homotopy relative to the entire coordinate boundary. Its reflexive, symmetric and transitive laws are supplied by constant homotopy, time reversal and concatenation, all retaining the boundary values. It therefore quotients by the intended based homotopy relation, not pointwise equality or free homotopy. Compared with [§4.1 p.340, based cubical homotopy classes; Proposition 1.2 p.26, equivalence-relation operations](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L256).

This instance asserts joint continuity of evaluation (f,y)↦f(y), not merely continuity at each fixed y. The generalized-loop space inherits the compact-open subspace topology, and Iᴺ is compact Hausdorff even for arbitrary N, so the evaluation theorem applies. Restricting evaluation along the continuous subtype inclusion gives the stated instance. Compared with [Proposition A.14(a), pp.530–531, joint evaluation continuity](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup.lean#L125).

The class requires every represented function I×X→Y to be continuous, with its time-zero and time-one slices equal to f₀ and f₁. These are exactly the homotopy conditions, abstracted over a function-like type so that extra constraints can share the API. It does not assert that this type contains a homotopy. Compared with [Chapter 0 p.3, definition of a homotopy; interval factor swapped](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L88).

The map sends t to the continuous time slice x↦F(t,x), with the compact-open topology on C(X,Y). This direction of currying is continuous for arbitrary X; Hatcher A.14(b) does not require local compactness. The existing endpoint lemmas recover f₀ and f₁, so no direction or endpoint is reversed. Compared with [Proposition A.14(b), pp.530–531, continuity of currying without local compactness](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L146).

Fixing x in a homotopy produces the path t↦H(t,x), from f(x) at time zero to g(x) at time one. Continuity is inherited by composing H with t↦(t,x), and the endpoint fields use exactly the homotopy endpoint laws. This is the actual trajectory of one point. Compared with [Chapter 0 pp.2–3, continuous point trajectories in a homotopy](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean#L452).

Precomposing a nullhomotopy of f:Y→Z by g:X→Y gives H(t,g(x)), ending at the same constant value in Z. The proof retains the original constant witness and composes the homotopy with the fixed map g. Thus the conclusion correctly concerns f∘g, with no assumption on the image of g. Compared with [Chapter 0 pp.3–4, homotopy and nullhomotopy definitions; the precomposition formula checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Contractible.lean#L38).

Postcomposing a nullhomotopy of f:X→Y by g:Y→Z gives g(H(t,x)), ending at the constant value g(y) when the original homotopy ends at y. This proves nullhomotopy of g∘f with the correct target witness; continuity of g is supplied by its continuous-map type. Compared with [Chapter 0 pp.3–4, homotopy and nullhomotopy definitions; the postcomposition formula checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Contractible.lean#L32).

The concatenation uses F on the first half of time and G on the second, agreeing at their shared map f₁. At any time its entire slice is a reparameterized slice of one input homotopy, so the same arbitrary predicate P remains true. No closure or continuity property of P is needed. Compared with [Proposition 1.2 p.26, time-concatenation construction; arbitrary slice predicate preservation checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L477).

Time reversal sends (t,x) to F(1−t,x), exchanging f₀ and f₁. Every reversed slice is an original slice, so any predicate P on the continuous map is preserved without further assumptions. The existing double-reversal identity confirms this is reversal of homotopy time. Compared with [Proposition 1.2 p.26, symmetry by time reversal](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L461).

A homotopy relative to S keeps each point of S fixed throughout time, so its initial and final maps agree at every x∈S. The proposition only assumes existence of such a homotopy and extracts the endpoint equality from it. It does not extend that equality outside S. Compared with [Chapter 0 p.3, definition of homotopy relative to a subspace](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Basic.lean#L641).

PreLp is the full dependent function space, before imposing any ℓᵖ condition. Its type synonym keeps the later ℓᵖ norm topology separate from the product topology. In particular no exponent, summability, boundedness or quotient by almost-everywhere equality appears in this definition. Compared with [the reference](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/01/09/245b-notes-3-lp-spaces/) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L342).

PreLp inherits the product ring structure of its coordinate rings, with pointwise operations. There is no boundedness restriction on the functions and no claim that this full product has a finite supremum norm. Infinite and empty index sets are allowed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.ucla.edu/~sharifi/notes/algebra-ch03.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L907).

SemilinearIsometryClass combines σ-semilinearity with exact preservation of the seminorm. Additivity turns this into preservation of distances. The seminormed setting permits zero-distance points, so the class does not incorrectly claim injectivity or surjectivity. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean#L67).

ContinuousSemilinearMapClass requires each bundled map to be σ-semilinear and continuous for the supplied topologies. It agrees with continuous linear maps when σ is the identity. It neither requires topological module operations nor identifies continuity with a norm bound. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L79).

Continuous σ-semilinear maps form an additive commutative group under pointwise operations. Continuity of target addition and negation gives closure; the group laws are inherited pointwise. No topological-group hypothesis on the domain is needed for this algebraic structure. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L842).

Continuous σ-semilinear maps form an additive commutative monoid when target addition is jointly continuous. Zero and addition are pointwise, and the monoid laws follow from the target laws. Additive inverses and scalar-ring commutativity are unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L438).

Addition of continuous σ-semilinear maps is pointwise addition. Joint continuity of target addition makes the sum continuous, while the module laws preserve σ-semilinearity. Both summands use the same scalar homomorphism σ. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L416).

Negation of a continuous σ-semilinear map is pointwise target negation. The target’s topological additive-group structure ensures continuity. It keeps the same scalar homomorphism σ, since scalar multiplication commutes with additive negation. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L818).

The zero continuous semilinear map is the constant function with value zero. It is continuous for every pair of topologies and is σ-semilinear for every supplied scalar homomorphism. No continuity assumption on module operations is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L325).

Taking the seminorm preserves convergence: if f tends to a, then ‖f‖ tends to ‖a‖. The seminorm is distance from zero, hence continuous. The actual hypothesis allows noncommutative additive groups and arbitrary source filters; no completeness or separation is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Continuity.lean#L189).

A seminormed additive commutative group has jointly continuous addition and continuous negation for its induced pseudometric topology. The source proves the stronger uniform continuity of subtraction first. Commutativity is present, and Hausdorff separation is unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Uniform.lean#L389).

For a fixed vector y, the scalar-action distance is bounded by dist(x₁,x₂)·dist(y,0). This is exactly the second defining estimate of IsBoundedSMul, exposed as a theorem. It gives a Lipschitz bound in the scalar variable without assuming norm homogeneity. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Algebra.lean#L130).

For a fixed scalar x, the action has Lipschitz bound dist(x,0) in the vector variable. This is the first defining IsBoundedSMul estimate. It is a distance inequality for a raw action on pointed pseudometric spaces, not an assertion of exact scalar norm homogeneity. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Algebra.lean#L127).

Continuity between pseudometric spaces is equivalent to the pointwise ε–δ condition. The positive δ may depend on both the point and ε, so this is ordinary continuity rather than uniform continuity. The statement needs no separation or completeness assumption. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/m127a_19/summary_topics_127a.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L886).

Convergence along atTop is equivalent to eventually lying in every positive-radius ball about the limit. A nonempty semilattice supplies directed upper tails. The cutoff condition n≥N is correct and works even if the index order has a greatest element. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/m127a_19/summary_topics_127a.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L910).

An eventual lower bound survives passage to a limit when upper rays are closed. The nontrivial-filter hypothesis is essential: a bottom filter would converge to every point and satisfy every eventual bound. The conclusion preserves a non-strict inequality, not strictness. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/m127a_19/summary_topics_127a.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean#L133).

If a limit v lies strictly below u, then the convergent function is eventually below u. Closed upper rays make the complementary strict lower ray open. The strict gap v<u is the hypothesis that ensures the limit lies in that neighbourhood. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/m127a_19/summary_topics_127a.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean#L237).

The upper ray [a,∞) is closed under the explicit ClosedIciTopology hypothesis. This theorem exposes that compatibility property; it does not claim that every topology on a preorder has closed rays. The endpoint is included. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean#L116).

For continuous f and g into an order-closed space, the set where f≤g is closed. The proof pulls back the closed order relation along x↦(f(x),g(x)). Requiring the full order relation to be closed is stronger than merely requiring individual rays to be closed. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean#L444).

The intersection of two closed subsets is closed in every topological space. Taking complements turns the intersection into a union of open sets. No separation, compactness or finiteness condition on the underlying space is needed.
